## Learning goals

By the end of this week, you should understand:

- how information is organized and delivered through websites;
- how researchers can collect information from static and interactive websites;
- why different websites require different data-collection strategies; and
- how technical choices affect the quality, completeness, and limitations of collected web data.

## Preparation before class

- Review the relevant sections of the Python Bootcamp.
- Make sure that you can access JupyterLab at [jupyterlab.uvt.nl](https://jupyterlab.uvt.nl/).
- Bring questions or problems encountered while working through the Python Bootcamp.

## Tutorials

### Web Scraping 101

This tutorial introduces the basic workflow for collecting data from webpages:

- sending requests;
- inspecting HTML;
- parsing webpages with Beautiful Soup;
- selecting elements and attributes; and
- transforming extracted values into a structured dataset.

### Web Scraping Advanced

This tutorial introduces browser automation with Selenium. You will practice:

- simulating selected user interactions;
- scrolling, clicking, and filling in forms;
- working with dynamically generated content; and
- saving collected results as JSON.

The advanced tutorial requires a local Python setup and is not designed for JupyterLab in the cloud.

## After class

- Work through the Web Scraping 101 and Web Scraping Advanced tutorials.
- Begin identifying a possible website or API for your team project.
- Register your project team on Canvas.
